_method.market: My own estimate of what the lot would realistically fetch today in a retail or well-attended auction setting -- not the house estimate, which on this sale runs ahead of the market in several categories. A range, because condition questions are still open on most of these.
_method.resale: What the buyer would actually NET if they had to let it go: regional auction hammer less a 20-25% seller's commission, or a refiner's 87% on melt-grade metal, or private/eBay net where that is the better route. This is the number the brief's real question turns on -- 'if I ever had to let it go, what do I lose?'
_method.melt: Weights are MY ESTIMATES from the form and the photographs. The scraped meta.json carries no weights and no descriptions, so not one figure here is a catalogued weight. Every one needs the scale at preview before it is treated as fact. Rates are the brief's deliberately conservative working spot; refiner net is 87%, the middle of the 85-90% band.
_method.gems: Secondary-market reality, not replacement value. Small melee diamonds, and coloured stones of this era that are routinely heat-treated or synthetic, recover very little on resale -- typically 10-30% of retail and often less. Where a stone is likely a doublet or composite it is called out.
